summary: Polygon's weekly roundup by Pete Volk of new streaming and rental movie releases for the weekend of November 3, 2023. The headline debut is Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse on Netflix, alongside Jawan, Insidious: The Red Door, Sly, Nyad and Wingwomen. Other picks include A Haunting in Venice on Hulu, Freaks vs. the Reich on Prime Video, and several rentals such as The Kill Room and Outlaw Johnny Black.
one_line: Polygon's weekend guide to new streaming and rental movies, led by Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse on Netflix and A Haunting in Venice on Hulu.
key_facts: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse is now streaming on Netflix; it runs 2h 20m and is directed by Joaquim Dos Santos, Kemp Powers and Justin K. Thompson.
In Across the Spider-Verse, Miles Morales faces the Spot and a multiverse of Spider-People, including a Spider-Dinosaur.
Jawan, directed by Atlee and starring Shah Rukh Khan, is the biggest Indian movie of the year, runs 2h 50m, and is described as "Robin Hood meets Charlie's Angels."
Insidious: The Red Door is the fifth Insidious movie, arrives on Netflix Saturday, and is the directorial debut of star Patrick Wilson; it is a sequel to Insidious: Chapter 2.
Sly is a 1h 35m Netflix documentary directed by Thom Zimny about Sylvester Stallone.
Nyad, directed by Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and starring Jodie Foster and Annette Bening, tells the story of Diana Nyad, who swam from Cuba to Florida at 64.
Wingwomen is a Netflix action comedy directed by and starring Mélanie Laurent about women thieves on the run.
A Haunting in Venice, directed by Kenneth Branagh, is streaming on Hulu and is called his best Poirot adaptation yet.
Quiz Lady on Hulu stars Awkwafina and Sandra Oh as estranged sisters trying to win a game show to pay off their mom's debts; Paul Reubens is in the supporting cast.
Freaks vs. the Reich, an Italian superhero movie by Gabriele Mainetti, is on Prime Video and follows circus performers in World War II who team up against the Nazis.
My Big Fat Greek Wedding 3 is on Peacock and is directed by Nia Vardalos, the first in the franchise since 2016.
Sympathy for the Devil, on AMC Plus, stars Nicolas Cage as a passenger who holds driver Joel Kinnaman hostage.
Outlaw Johnny Black is Michael Jai White's follow-up to Black Dynamite, a "West-ploitation" movie about an outlaw posing as a preacher.
Sound of Freedom, available to rent, is described as one of the year's most surprising and controversial box-office hits, purporting to be a true story about stopping child trafficking.
